guidelines.detail: documentation rule PROC-05 not applied (The description explicitly says to stop the process when the machine is disconnected, while the validator reports that the process has no end event. Documented guideline PROC-05 already requires every process to have an explicit end event.)

refines PROC-05 (The description states that measuring continues after a restart (S3). The reference represents that continuation as an activity (M4), while the generated model uses an unmatched start event (X1). This refines PROC-05 by specifying how to model a later trigger that resumes ongoing work.)

same as LRN-065 (The description says measuring continues when the machine is restarted. The records show that the reference represents this continuation as an activity (M4), while the generated model instead has a start event with no reference counterpart (X1). This supports correcting the BPMN element choice, not adding an otherwise missing action. The wording is process-independent and matches learned guideline)

documentation rule EVT-02 not applied (The description says the process stops when the machine is disconnected, while the validator reports that the process has no end event. This supports modeling the stated termination explicitly. Documented guideline EVT-02 already says to use end events for terminal outcomes.)

same as LRN-065 (The description states that measuring continues when the machine is restarted. The reference models that continuation as an activity, while the generated model uses an unmatched start event; this guideline prevents that mismatch. It is essentially the same as learned guideline LRN-065.)

refines FID-04 (The description gives a threshold condition but no numeric cutoff, while the generated gateway label adds one. This refines FID-04 by specifying how to avoid guessing in this threshold-labeling situation.)

documentation rule PROC-05 not applied (The validator reports that the process has no end event, and the description explicitly says it stops when the machine is disconnected. PROC-05 already requires every process to have an explicit end event, so this guideline restates an existing rule.)

same as LRN-065 (The description states that measuring continues when the machine is restarted. The reference models that continuation as an activity connected from the restart, while the generated model has an extra start event and omits the activity and its incoming flow. This supports the learned guideline LRN-065.)

same as LRN-066 (The reference label adds a specific cutoff that the description does not provide. The generated label avoids that unsupported detail; this guideline captures the supported lesson and is already stated essentially the same way in LRN-066.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the process terminates when a specified condition occurs

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that work in an ongoing process resumes after a later trigger: model the trigger within the existing process and represent the stated continuation as an activity, rather than as a new process start
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that work in an ongoing process resumes after a later trigger

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a condition or event that terminates the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description specifies a threshold-based condition but does not state its numeric cutoff: Label the corresponding gateway with the stated condition without adding an unsupported numeric cutoff.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description specifies a threshold-based condition but does not state its numeric cutoff
